comments.text:
2:20 I'm very physically disabled today, but back when I wasn't, I was very active. VERY active. Got my first concussion when I was like 5 or 6 years old but it was the 90s lol. And guess what sport I was playing? Soccer lol.

Through out my life, I accumulated 5 concussions. 2 were from soccer, and like 1.5 concussions from football lol. The other half of the concussion was actually me taking repeated basketballs to the face during my school gym class because I got hit in the head in a morning football practice and no one noticed how hard I actually got hit. Then due to a lack of hand eye coordination from that mornings hit, I couldn't catch the basketball. And it only occured to me the third time... And also the entire gym class going to get the teacher. It was known I was very athletic, so missing a simple basketball pass 3 times consecutively, something was wrong lol.

My last concussion was in 2013, snowboarding for the first time. I still have Brain damage today. An interruption of turning a thought into words (and that's why I use so many freaking words lol. If I don't text this way, I can't text at all). Plus when I gently shake my head no, even today, I can feel a shot of pain exactly where it was I landed on it... 13 years later.

Concussions are no joke peeps. They are life altering, even minor concussions

Edit* its true that when concussed, you are not able to think straight. One of my soccer concussions was during an indoor game where another player accidentally headbutted the base of my skull as we both jumped to head the ball. My memory still tells me that I stood there looking down the field and it was empty. What ACTUALLY happened is that I stumbled to the boards for something to hold onto. The field was full of 2 teams worth of players, and I was looking directly at the crowd stands behind the boards.
comments.author: @PureNrGG

comments.text:
12:00 that "other player" is the same player as the one you commented on right now. Danish superstar Christian Eriksen. He was still playing high level football eversince his first episode, considering he was wearing an Implantable Cardioverter Defibrilator. He had to transfer from his former club Internazzionale Milano because the legislation in Italy didnt allow him keep playing in the new conditions in Italy, so he transfered to a smaller, newly promoted, i think, club in the Brittish Premier League: Brentford. Then he proved to still be very capable of playing high level, although not exactly as good as he once was, but enough for Manchester United to offer him a deal. Spent a few years there and since last summer moved to German Bundesliga, 1st tier in Germany, at Wolfsburg. So he was still playing top level for 3-4 years or so since the almost tragic event. 

Now, what happened here is that he most likely had a ventricular arythmia and that ICD detected it right in time and shocked him, and that is why he put his hands to his heart. He was back up after a few minutes and reassured everyone on social media he was ok very soon afterwards. Don't know if he announced he had enough by now, but everyone is kinda expecting him to quit in this season break.
